channel.title: 3D Printing Legislation Tracker
channel.description: Updates from the 3D Printing Weekly meetup's community tracker of 3D printer and 3D-printed firearm legislation.

item.title: AB 2047 is law: signed Sep 26, dormant until ASTM acts
item.description: Governor Newsom signed AB 2047 on Sep 26 (Chapter 461, Statutes of 2026). It takes effect Jan 1, 2027, but the printer sale ban only starts if ASTM International publishes a blocking-tech standard and the CA DOJ writes rules: mid-2028 at the very earliest, realistically 2030 or later, possibly never. The card now covers owners, used sales, gifts, self-built machines and businesses. Take Action has a new "Get in before the standard exists" panel, and the letter generator now writes to the CA DOJ.

item.title: AB 2047 presented to Governor Newsom — decision by Sep 30
item.description: AB 2047 was formally enrolled and presented to Governor Newsom on Sep 14 at 1:30 p.m. He must act by Sep 30: sign, veto, or the bill becomes law without his signature — California has no pocket veto. The card's timeline, details, and verification date are updated.

item.title: New: the Prop Problem tab, and what ASTM actually is
item.description: The Prop Problem now has its own tab — why shape-detection algorithms and Star Wars prop blasters can't coexist, with examples from our own members' testing. The Blocking Technology tab gains a plain-language explainer of ASTM International, the standards body California's AB 2047 hangs on.

item.title: Tracker launched — AB 2047 is on Newsom's desk
item.description: The tracker goes live with 12 cards: California AB 2047 (passed the legislature Aug 31, 60-18 concurrence; Governor Newsom signs or vetoes by end of September), New York's signed blocking-tech law, Washington's HB 2320 (in force) and stalled HB 2321, New Jersey's file-possession law, Colorado HB26-1144, the serialization wave, the US federal baseline, and the UK, Australia, Canada, and EU.
